headline: Banned Awami League activists stage armed rally, vandalise property in Gopalganj

members.title: Banned Awami League activists stage armed rally, vandalise property in Gopalganj
members.lead: Activists of Awami League, whose activities are currently banned, and its affiliated organisations staged a procession and rally in Gopalganj carrying local weapons, including bamboo poles, oars, machetes and Chinese axes. During the procession, they vandalised a police armoured personnel carrier (APC) and a police box. They also damaged the July Memorial and the nameplate at Hadi Chattar. The activists staged processions along various roads in Gopalganj town from 11am to 1:45pm on Sunday. Many of them were seen carrying traditional weapons, including bamboo poles, sticks, machetes, Chinese axes, spears and tridents. Some were wearing helmets. They also chanted various slogans. . Local sources said activists from different unions began arriving at Ghosherchar Uttarpara in Latifpur union of Sadar Upazila at around 8am. Food was arranged for them at the house of Salauddin Khan, organising secretary of the banned municipal Awami League. . They then went to Gabtala intersection. Led by Salauddin, the activists marched through the BSCIC Bridge and entered the town. Meanwhile, another procession was brought out from Ghosherchar Dakshinpara, led by banned Chhatra League leader Md Samiul Haque. A separate procession also started from the Mia and Nabinbagh areas of the town under the leadership of former councillor Alamin. The processions converged near the Old Launch Ghat Bridge. The activists then marched to the district Awami League office in Bankpara. They opened the office, which had remained locked for a long time, and celebrated. According to eyewitnesses, the activists vandalised the July Memorial near the Gopalganj Launch Ghat while marching through the area. They then erased the nameplate at the main entrance of Gopalganj Government College and put up a banner bearing the name ‘Government Bangabandhu College’. members.title: Gopalganj DC, SP removed from their posts
members.lead: The Deputy Commissioner (DC) of Gopalganj, Md Arif-Uz-Zaman, has been withdrawn and attached to the Ministry of Public Administration. The government has appointed Habiganj's DC, GM Sarfaraz, as the new Deputy Commissioner of this district. Additionally, the Superintendent of Police (SP) of Gopalganj, Md Habibullah, has also been transferred. He has been appointed as the SP of Feni. Meanwhile, the current SP of Feni, Pratyush Kumar Majumdar, has been appointed as the new SP of Gopalganj. . This information was announced today, Sunday, in separate circulars by the Ministry of Public Administration and the Ministry of Home Affairs. Today, leaders and activists of the Awami League, whose activities now banned, held processions on various roads in Gopalganj town. . During this time, many were seen carrying local weapons, including sticks, rods, machetes, Chinese axes, spears, and clubs. Some wore helmets while conducting their demonstrations. They chanted various slogans. .Banned Awami League activists stage armed rally, vandalise property in Gopalganj. In the midst of this situation, the government has made changes to the top two positions of administration and police in Gopalganj. Meanwhile, Zakir Hossain, Deputy Secretary of the Cabinet Division, has been appointed as the DC of Habiganj. Md Alamgir Kabir, Deputy Secretary of the Ministry of Public Administration, has been appointed as the DC of Chuadanga.

members.title: Banned AL men stage armed rally in Gopalganj, vandalise structures
members.lead: Banned Awami League, Jubo League, Chhatra League activists and affiliated groups staged an armed procession and rally in Gopalganj, carrying oars, boat poles, and machetes. They vandalised the July Memorial, a nameplate at Hadi Chattar, an armoured police vehicle, and a police box.
